comparison: Both evaluate AutoMitoC method validation (C18-C23). OpenEval finds validation correlations statistically significant and performance consistent, rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers request more thorough benchmarking, noting 'moderate' correlation magnitude and insufficient method description, rating UNCERTAIN.

Both address mtDNA-CN associations with predictors (C24-C28). OpenEval finds comprehensive characterization with highly significant associations (p<10^-47), rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers request more detailed phenotype description and distribution analysis, particularly for age and sex effects, rating UNCERTAIN.

OpenEval evaluates full set of predictor associations (C24-C35) as SUPPORTED. Peer R3 focuses on cell composition confounding (C29-C35) and accepts adjustment approach as SUPPORTED, though emphasizes need to discuss this caveat.

Both evaluate primary GWAS results (C36-C44). OpenEval finds appropriate quality control and statistical thresholds with minimal population stratification, rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept GWAS as 'robust' and 'fairly standard' with convincing results, rating SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate fine-mapping results (C45-C54). OpenEval finds FINEMAP methodology appropriate with biological validation from mtDNA depletion gene overlap, rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept fine-mapping and enrichment findings, noting reproducibility across studies, rating SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate enrichment of mtDNA depletion genes (C55-C59). OpenEval finds 53% enrichment statistically meaningful despite suggestive threshold, rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept enrichment as supporting evidence and note reproducibility, rating SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate comparison with prior studies (C60-C67). OpenEval finds partial replication expected given methodological differences, rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers request more thorough comparison, particularly with Longchamps 2021, to place work in context, rating UNCERTAIN.

Both evaluate transethnic consistency (C68-C69). OpenEval finds high correlations support generalizability but notes sample size imbalances limit interpretation, rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers request more discussion of population structure confounding, rating UNCERTAIN.

Both evaluate mt-eQTL integration (C70-C74). OpenEval finds overlap provides mechanistic insight but notes causality direction unclear, rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers question the rationale and request clearer explanation of directionality testing, rating UNCERTAIN.

Both evaluate heteroplasmy GWAS overlap (C75-C79). OpenEval finds concordant directionality supports shared genetic basis, rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers request clear rationale for comparison and biological interpretation, rating UNCERTAIN.

Both evaluate pathway enrichment (C80-C89). OpenEval finds significant MT-related GO term enrichment but notes PPRC1 coordinator role is speculative, rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept enrichment findings but request statistical tests comparing proportions to MitoCarta baseline, rating SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate MitoCarta3 annotations (C87-C89). OpenEval finds enrichments statistically significant with modest p-value for PGC-1A (0.04), rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept findings as part of broader pathway validation, requesting additional statistical comparisons, rating SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate ExWAS results (C90-C95). OpenEval finds SAMHD1 exome-wide significant with appropriate correction, rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept ExWAS findings as study strength, noting rare variant analysis contribution, rating SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate PheWAS results (C96-C100). OpenEval finds phenome-wide significance with appropriate sensitivity analyses, rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept SAMHD1-cancer findings as robust contribution, rating SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate MR analysis (C101-C109). OpenEval finds consistency across methods with appropriate sensitivity tests, though replication p-value barely significant (0.04993), rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers find MR 'superficial' and 'unconvincing,' requesting more thorough pleiotropy testing with HEIDI and comparative analysis, rating UNCERTAIN.

Both evaluate biological interpretation of genetic findings (C110-C112, C6-C7, C141). OpenEval finds interpretation well-supported by pathway analyses, rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept overall genetic architecture interpretation as 'real biology' and 'robust,' rating SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate SAMHD1 clinical implications (C113-C122). OpenEval finds integration with established knowledge appropriate with speculative therapeutic suggestions clearly marked, rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept interpretations as reasonable implications and note druggable target potential, rating SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate MR contextualization and dementia findings (C123-C130). OpenEval finds 'first MR evidence' claim accurate with appropriate synthesis, rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers acknowledge novelty but express concerns about MR strength, emphasizing 'may play a role' rather than definitive causation, rating UNCERTAIN.

Both evaluate study limitations (C131-C140, C142-C144). OpenEval finds limitations appropriately acknowledged with mitigation steps taken, rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers appreciate limitation acknowledgment but request more thorough discussion of caveats, particularly cell composition and population structure, rating SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates concluding synthesis (C141-C144) as appropriately acknowledging complexity and uncertainty, rating SUPPORTED. Peer R15 addresses broader interpretation including C141, accepting genetic architecture characterization as robust, rating SUPPORTED.

OpenEval identifies discrepancy between abstract claim of 71 loci (C1-C2) and results describing 70 loci after NUMT filtering, rating UNCERTAIN. Peer R4 accepts the 71 loci finding as part of robust GWAS results, rating SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate key SAMHD1 findings (C3-C4). OpenEval finds associations highly significant with appropriate effect sizes, rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept SAMHD1 findings as major contribution showing rare variants associated with cancer risk, rating SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate primary MR finding (C5). OpenEval finds evidence supports likely causal relationship with appropriate sensitivity tests, rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers find MR analysis superficial with unconvincing pleiotropy testing, rating UNCERTAIN.

Both evaluate overarching conclusions (C6-C7). OpenEval finds C6 well-supported by pathway analyses, C7 supported for dementia but uncertain for other diseases, rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept genetic architecture interpretation as robust, rating SUPPORTED.
